subject: general
question: Which of the following subjects is addressed by the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Provisions related to anti-defection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tenth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution was added by the **52nd Amendment Act of 1985** and is popularly known as the **Anti-Defection Law**.
 
• It contains provisions to prevent **political defection** by Members of Parliament (MPs) and Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs).
 
• The primary aim of the Tenth Schedule is to ensure **political stability** by discouraging elected representatives from switching parties for personal gains.
 
• Under the Anti-Defection Law, a member can be disqualified if they **voluntarily give up the membership of their party** or vote against the party's directive without prior permission.
 
• The decision regarding disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is made by the **Speaker or Chairman** of the respective House, whose decision is subject to judicial review.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anti-Defection Law:**

 
 
• The **Anti-Defection Law** was enacted to address the issue of instability caused by defections by legislators after elections.
 
• The law applies to both Parliament and State Legislatures in India.
 
• A legislator is deemed to have defected if they **join another party**, abstain from voting on key issues against their party's directives, or voluntarily give up their party membership.
 
• Exemptions are made for merger cases where at least **two-thirds of the members** of a party agree to merge with another party.
 
 
 
• **Role of Speaker/Chairman:**
 
 
• The Speaker or Chairman of the House decides on disqualification cases under the Anti-Defection Law.
 
• While their decision is final, it is subject to **judicial review**, ensuring accountability.
 
• There have been instances where the judiciary intervened in cases of delayed or biased decisions under the law.
 
 
 
• **Challenges and Criticism:**
 
 
• The law has been criticized for not addressing the issue of internal democracy within political parties.
 
• It has been observed that party leaderships often misuse the law to suppress dissent within the party.
 
• Delay in decision-making by presiding officers has often led to political instability.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Anti-Defection Law plays a crucial role in ensuring the **stability of governments** and promoting loyalty to party ideologies.
 
• It prevents unscrupulous practices like horse-trading of legislators and unethical political alliances.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Tenth Schedule was introduced in **1985** during the tenure of Prime Minister **Rajiv Gandhi**.
 
• The law has been amended several times to address evolving political challenges.
 
• Judicial review has emerged as a critical aspect of ensuring the proper implementation of the Anti-Defection Law.
 
• While the law has largely succeeded in curbing defections, critics argue that it needs further reform to enhance the democratic functioning of political institutions.
